@@U01708@@
But that’s not fair!

@@U01710@@
And even if she gets him, it'll be no picnic for her. The boys'll rip off her bridal garland, and we'll strew straw at her door for the shame of her.

@@U01711@@
(Exit.)

@@U01713@@
(Walking home.)

@@U01714@@
Time was Id rail with the best of them about some poor girl who went wrong. There were never words enough for the sins of others. They seemed so black, and I made them even blacker; but even then it wasn’t black enough for me. I'd bless myself then and feel so proud— and now I’m just as bad as them. And yet, everything that drove me to it— O God! How good it was, how good, how sweet!

@@U01716@@
An image of the Mater Dolorosa（痛苦圣母） set in the niche of a wall with pots of flowers in front of it. 格蕾琴 puts fresh flowers into them.

@@U01718@@
Mother of Sorrows, behold me in my distress! Your heart pierced by the sword knows unending pain as you look on your Son dying.
translation:
@@U01708@@
但这不公平！

@@U01710@@
即使她得到了他，对她来说也不是一件容易的事。男孩们会扯下她的新娘花环，我们会在她的门口撒上稻草来羞辱她。

@@U01711@@
（退出。）

@@U01713@@
（步行回家。）

@@U01714@@
我曾向他们中最优秀的人抱怨某个可怜的女孩犯了错误。对于别人的罪孽，言语永远都不够。它们看起来很黑，我把它们弄得更黑；但即便如此，它对我来说还不够黑。那时我会祝福自己并感到非常自豪——而现在我和他们一样糟糕。然而，一切驱使我这么做的——上帝啊！多么美好，多么美好，多么甜蜜！

@@U01716@@
墙上的壁龛里有一尊痛苦圣母像，前面放着花盆。 格蕾琴将鲜花放入其中。

@@U01718@@
悲伤之母，看我陷入困境！当你看着你的儿子死去时，你被剑刺穿的心会感到无尽的痛苦。
